questions.prompt: A top-level secure page needs cross-origin isolation and serves COOP same-origin. Which conventional additional response policy completes the isolation policy pair?

sources.title: HTML Standard: Browsers
sources.claim: The conventional pair is COOP same-origin plus COEP require-corp. Embedded resources must satisfy the resulting loading restrictions. CORS, referrer and cache headers alone do not substitute for the embedder policy.

questions.explanation: The conventional pair is COOP same-origin plus COEP require-corp. Embedded resources must satisfy the resulting loading restrictions. CORS, referrer and cache headers alone do not substitute for the embedder policy.

choices.text: Access-Control-Allow-Origin wildcard, without any embedder policy.
Referrer-Policy no-referrer, without any embedder policy.
COEP require-corp, with compatible resource loading.
Cache-Control no-store, without any embedder policy.

questions.prompt: A page preloads a font but the later font fetch uses a different credentials mode. Why might the browser fetch it again?

sources.title: HTML Standard: Links and preloads
sources.claim: The preload cache matches relevant request properties such as destination and credentials mode. A mismatch can prevent reuse. Preload does fetch data, but reuse is neither always impossible nor guaranteed by URL alone.

questions.explanation: The preload cache matches relevant request properties such as destination and credentials mode. A mismatch can prevent reuse. Preload does fetch data, but reuse is neither always impossible nor guaranteed by URL alone.

choices.text: A preload always forces a second fetch regardless of its later request properties.
Font preloads are display instructions and never fetch any resource bytes.
The preload URL alone guarantees reuse even when request modes differ.
Reuse requires matching request properties, including credentials mode.

questions.prompt: A bubbling, composed event originates inside a shadow tree and reaches an outside listener. Which event rules hold? Select all that apply.

sources.title: DOM Standard: Event dispatch and retargeting
sources.claim: A and B describe composed propagation and retargeting. D: the composed path hides closed-tree internals from outside observers. C confuses bubbling with composition; E is false because currentTarget is the object whose listener is executing.

questions.explanation: A and B describe composed propagation and retargeting. D: the composed path hides closed-tree internals from outside observers. C confuses bubbling with composition; E is false because currentTarget is the object whose listener is executing.

choices.text: The event can cross the shadow boundary because it is composed.
Outside listeners can observe a retargeted target at the shadow host.
Bubbles alone guarantees that every event crosses every shadow boundary.
A closed shadow root limits what outside composedPath exposes.
Retargeting changes every outside listener currentTarget to the inner element.

questions.prompt: A page enables COEP require-corp and an opaque cross-origin image lacks permission to be embedded. What behavior should the team anticipate?

sources.title: HTML Standard: Browsers
sources.claim: COEP imposes loading restrictions; resources need appropriate CORP or a suitable CORS fetch. It cannot rewrite remote server headers, change an origin or automatically proxy content.

questions.explanation: COEP imposes loading restrictions; resources need appropriate CORP or a suitable CORS fetch. It cannot rewrite remote server headers, change an origin or automatically proxy content.

choices.text: The browser automatically proxies the image through the page origin.
The policy forces the remote server to add a CORP header to its response.
The image becomes same-origin because the page opted into isolation.
The embedder policy can block that image from loading.

questions.prompt: A page preloads a script resource with a link element. What does that preload do by itself?

sources.title: HTML Standard: Links and preloads
sources.claim: Preload obtains a resource for later use; it does not execute scripts, populate global bindings or rewrite later script elements by itself.

questions.explanation: Preload obtains a resource for later use; it does not execute scripts, populate global bindings or rewrite later script elements by itself.

choices.text: Fetch the resource early without executing it as a script.
Execute the script immediately as soon as its first bytes reach the browser.
Install every function in the global scope before the script request completes.
Replace all subsequent script elements with their source text automatically.

questions.prompt: A component dispatches `new Event('status', {bubbles: true, composed: false})` from an internal shadow element. Which claims are correct? Select all that apply.

sources.title: DOM Standard: Event dispatch and retargeting
sources.claim: B: non-composed dispatch stays within the relevant shadow boundary. D enables boundary crossing. A is false because bubbling still works internally. C is false because the flags serve different purposes; E is false because dispatch does not rename the type.

questions.explanation: B: non-composed dispatch stays within the relevant shadow boundary. D enables boundary crossing. A is false because bubbling still works internally. C is false because the flags serve different purposes; E is false because dispatch does not rename the type.

choices.text: The event cannot bubble inside the shadow tree when composed is false.
The event does not cross that shadow root solely because bubbles is true.
Every document listener receives the event because bubbles overrides composed.
Setting composed true would permit propagation across the shadow boundary.
The event automatically changes its type to the shadow host element name.
